intro: A quadratic equation has the form ax² + bx + c = 0 with a ≠ 0. Its solutions are called roots. We find roots by factorisation or by the quadratic formula, and the discriminant tells us the nature of the roots without solving.
keyPoints: Standard form: ax² + bx + c = 0, a ≠ 0.
Factorisation: split the middle term so that the two parts multiply to ac and add to b.
D > 0: two distinct real roots. D = 0: two equal real roots. D < 0: no real roots.

examples.title: Nature of roots
examples.problem: Find the nature of the roots of 2x² − 4x + 3 = 0.

examples.title: Word problem
examples.problem: Find two consecutive positive integers whose product is 306.
steps: Let the integers be x and x + 1: x(x + 1) = 306
x = 17 (x = −18 is rejected because it is not positive)
